one_liner: Zero-copy Rust parser-combinator crate, forked from nom, favoring API evolution and built-in features over strict compatibility.
what_it_does: winnow builds parsers for text and binary formats out of composable combinators, the same problem nom solves. It is a hard fork of nom's codebase but is not a drop-in replacement: parsers are written against a `Parser<I, O, E>` trait rather than nom's `FnMut(I) -> IResult<I, O, E>` closures, and many combinators are renamed (doc aliases point back to the nom names). It supports zero-copy parsing, streaming (partial) input, and both byte- and char-oriented grammars.
how_it_is_fast: The library is byte-oriented and zero-copy by default; its own performance docs recommend parsing as `u8` rather than `char` and using `dispatch` instead of `alt` when branches have unique prefixes, to cut per-token overhead. An optional `simd` feature pulls in `memchr` for accelerated byte/substring search. winnow deliberately avoids Rust GATs (which nom v8 uses for call-site specialization), trading a slice of peak throughput for more predictable performance and simpler generated code (smaller `impl Trait` return types, faster builds).
when_to_use: Already writing or migrating a nom-style combinator parser and want ongoing feature development rather than nom's stability-first churn policy
Parsing bytes/binary formats where zero-copy slices and streaming (partial-input) parsing matter
Willing to enable the `simd` feature (adds `memchr`) for token/substring-heavy grammars
Want built-in extras (debug tracing, `dispatch`, bit-level parsing, error recovery groundwork) without pulling in separate nom-ecosystem crates
no_std / no-alloc embedded targets, using the crate's `alloc`/`std` feature flags to scope in only what's needed
when_not_to_use: Need a drop-in nom replacement with zero migration cost — API is renamed and trait-based, not source-compatible

Basing the choice purely on the winnow-vs-nom speed number: it comes from a competing project's (chumsky) README table, not winnow's own benchmark suite, and was not independently reproduced this session

Need the single fastest option in this category — chumsky's own bench shows chumsky itself beating winnow (140.77 us / 797 MB/s check-only, 210.43 us / 533 MB/s full parse, vs winnow's 178.91 us / 627 MB/s) on the same workload
Require documented thread-safety guarantees — none are stated in the README or docs pages read
Need nom v8's GAT-based call-site specialization for squeezing out extra throughput in hot, tightly-controlled parsers

integration.dependencies: none required; optional memchr (simd feature), optional anstream/anstyle/is_terminal_polyfill/terminal_size (debug feature)
integration.platforms: any (pure Rust; alloc/std feature-gated for no_std use)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — hard fork of nom's code and concepts, but combinators are renamed and parsers implement a `Parser` trait instead of nom's `FnMut(I) -> IResult` closures; migration guide and doc-aliases exist but source is not compatible

gotchas: Char-based parsing is measurably slower than byte-based per the project's own performance notes; parse `u8` and use `BStr` only for debug display
Chained combinators can produce large inferred types that slow builds; the docs recommend wrapping chains in a closure or naming them to avoid `impl Trait` bloat
`simd` feature must be opted into (`cargo add winnow -F simd`) to get memchr-accelerated search; it is not on by default
GitHub's license badge shows NOASSERTION, but LICENSE-MIT, Cargo.toml, and the COPYRIGHT file all state MIT
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick winnow over chumsky when you want a nom-style imperative combinator API and an incremental migration path from an existing nom parser, not the top raw throughput — chumsky's own benchmark shows chumsky itself outrunning winnow on the same JSON workload. Pick it over MPL/FastParse when you need a mature, widely-used, actively maintained general-purpose crate rather than a newer project whose README leads with beating winnow specifically.
verified_claims_summary: On chumsky's own idiomatic single-document JSON benchmark (single core, AMD Ryzen 7 3700x, cargo bench with debug=true, rustc version/flags unstated), winnow parsed at 178.91 us (627 MB/s) versus nom at 526.52 us (213 MB/s), about 2.9x the throughput. The table lives in chumsky's README (mirrored on Codeberg), not in winnow's own docs or benchmarks, and was not rerun independently this session.
status_note: Actively maintained (default-branch commit 2026-09-17, frequent releases per crates.io versioning in Cargo.toml); MIT-licensed and published as an ordinary crate, so it is easy to vendor or pin despite the GitHub license-detector showing NOASSERTION.
